assumptions: This predicate concerns the selected applicability condition, not whole-law compliance or licence possession.
Case-dependent input classifications and incorporated authority remain external to the encoded predicate.
The declared input vocabulary is supplied for this controlled comparison; its adequacy as a legal abstraction remains unverified.
The supplied ra13_context fact represents the actor and in-course-of-RA13 conditions together; the supplied in_hong_kong fact represents the receipt-or-holding territorial condition.
The phrase “regardless of the role played by such LC” makes transfer-agent status immaterial to the selected trigger; it does not dispense with the preceding conditions.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, regardless of the role played by such LC.
That said, in the context of RA 13, handling of money which is not “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong will not be subject to the CMR.

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

hypothesis.aa7fd773229909b178076920.distinction: Considered two attachments: “regardless” qualifies the main applicability assertion, or qualifies the immediately preceding description of conducting RA13. Both leave the actor, scheme-money and Hong Kong conditions intact and make the LC's role immaterial. A transfer-agent exclusion or a reading that role independence removes the RA13 condition lacks textual support. Only one distinct Boolean reading is defensible for this target. The separate negation ambiguity in the following paragraph does not alter that affirmative trigger.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, regardless of the role played by such LC.

Generally, the relevant period starts on the day when the receipt1 by the RA 13 LC in Hong Kong becomes scheme money of any relevant CIS.

hypothesis.b2a2ae3e60f7915cf1d72186.distinction: Candidate attachments considered are role independence within the expressly qualified applicability proposition, role independence overriding the Type 13 activity condition, and restriction of applicability to transfer agents because Q1 asks about them. Only the first is defensible: “regardless” removes role as an additional condition while preserving the express money, location and activity qualifications. The question's transfer-agent example cannot narrow the answer's general wording. Schedule 11 expectations and Q2's payment timing do not change that attachment. A single reading is therefore retained.

concerns.question: The in_hong_kong definition presupposes scheme money. It cannot cleanly express the location of non-scheme money, which matters when distinguishing narrow and broad negation in Q1's second paragraph.
The vocabulary contains no facts for Schedule 11 duties, their relevance, or compliance; the predicate cannot decide those matters or equate “expected to observe” with an encoded unconditional duty.

The combined ra13_context fact cannot separately test actor identity, receipt or holding by the LC or AE, and the connection to the LC's RA13 activity. Its adequacy remains an external classification assumption.
The incorporated legal definitions and the missing dependency are not supplied in full. The scheme_money fact preserves that external judgment rather than resolving it.

In Q1's second paragraph, does “not” negate only “scheme money”, with “received or held in Hong Kong” qualifying the money, or the entire description “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong? These parses may affect the stated reach of the Schedule 11 expectation, but neither supplies a transfer-agent exception to the affirmative applicability trigger.
ra13_context compresses actor identity, associated-entity status, handling and the activity nexus; “handling” does not independently establish the source's receipt-or-holding requirement.
in_hong_kong is defined for scheme money, so its meaning for non-scheme money is unspecified. It cannot reliably distinguish rival scopes of the subsequent negative sentence for all funds.
The vocabulary cannot encode Schedule 11 expectations, their relevant paragraphs, or compliance with them. These remain separate from the Q1 predicate.

The vocabulary cannot represent receipt dates, unknown-receipt evidence, account ownership, REIT-property status or the qualified assessment “unlikely to be considered”. Those matters may inform external classifications but cannot be independently tested here.

What incorporated definitions and missing dependency determine whether funds are scheme money received or held by the LC or its AE? Those classifications cannot be resolved from the supplied vocabulary alone.

Does “not ‘scheme money’ received or held in Hong Kong” negate scheme-money status alone or the combined status-and-location condition? This may affect the surrounding exclusion and Schedule 11 discussion, but does not supply a defensible rival to the affirmative Q1 trigger.
